ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended, effective 1 January 2021); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024); Measures for the Administration of Registration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (as amended) for governing the Taiwanese investor's beneficial interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese notary public followed by either (a) Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China if used in an Apostille Convention state; (b) Consular Legalization at a Chinese Embassy/Consulate if used in a non-member state; or (c) Cross-Strait Notarization-Verification through SEF/ARATS if used in Taiwan. These paths are mutually exclusive; do not combine Apostille and Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Domicile Qualification Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / Municipal SAMR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same three-tier parallel path: Chinese notary plus Apostille for Apostille members; Chinese notary plus Consular Legalization for non-members; SEF/ARATS verification for Taiwan. Never chain Apostille and Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing service agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the WFOE / sole shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by, depending on destination, either Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China, Consular Legalization by a Chinese consulate, or SEF/ARATS verification for Taiwan. Select only one path; do not chain.

Notarized; then either Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China for Hague member states, Consular Legalization for non-member states, or SEF/ARATS verification for Taiwan. Paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese commercial bank maintaining the shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by bank branch, notarized, then either Apostille (Hague member state) or Consular Legalization (non-member state); for Taiwan, use local notarization plus SEF/ARATS verification. Apostille and Consular Legalization are not cumulative.
Notarized and filed with SAMR/PBOC under Order No. 3; no Apostille or Consular Legalization required for domestic use; if used in Taiwan, cross-strait SEF/ARATS verification may apply.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation and at any subsequent ownership change, the WFOE and every Taiwanese beneficial owner must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HMT UK Sanctions List, and Chinese Ministry of Public Security/PBOC watchlists. PEPs, including mainland Chinese officials and Taiwanese political figures, require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source-of-wealth documentation, and semi-annual monitoring. Negative hits trigger immediate suspension and frozen filings.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and Enterprise Name Registration Platform of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE shall have a mandatory Chinese name in simplified Chinese characters. The foreign (Taiwanese) investor's corporate name must be transliterated phonetically into Mandarin Pinyin within the four-tier naming convention: administrative division + distinct name + industry description + company form. No Latin letters or non-Chinese characters may be used unless separately approved by SAMR. The chosen name cannot infringe prior identical or similar registered marks and must contain at least one distinguishing term.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, SAMR issues a written refusal with statutory reasoning. The applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration appeal with the municipal-level SAMR within 15 working days, or an administrative lawsuit with the competent People's Court within 6 months. The appeal must identify the objectionable token and propose a revised name preserving the four-tier structure. A reconsideration decision is expected within 30 working days; no new fee is payable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual mail-forwarding or commercial mailbox address is not accepted as the registered office for a WFOE supplying international media relations and public relations services. SAMR requires a physical address in a lawful commercial building, and the local tax authority rejects virtual offices because the enterprise lacks actual employees, lease, and operational substance. Shared or serviced office space is allowed only with a genuine sublease, access control record, and evidence of daily business operations; otherwise the WFOE is at risk of classification as a shell company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist: SAMR address verification; local tax bureau on-site examination; labor and social insurance presence check; fire safety and environmental review; verification of signage, lease receipts, and workforce counts. Quantified risk: 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months for a low-risk service WFOE; 40% probability if the registered address is shared with three or more unrelated entities or if the shareholder is a foreign-contributed entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), as amended and codified in the laws of Taiwan, particularly Chapter III (limited company) and Chapter V (company limited by shares), Articles 1, 5, 6, 15, 18, 98-113, 128-227, 387, 412, 419, 423 and 445; Foreign Investment by Foreign Nationals Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 7-10; and, if the immediate investor is a Mainland China-controlled entity, the Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by People from Mainland Area.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commerce Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, operating through the MOEA One-Stop Company and Commercial Registration portal; foreign capital admission is separately approved by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company Limited by Shares (股份有限公司設立登記申請書), filed with the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), CPA Capital Verification Report (會計師資本查核報告書), and certified minutes of the First Board of Directors meeting.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None formally: Taiwan Company Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow-account requirement for an ISIC 7310 public-relations/communications WFOE. The capital stated in the Investment Commission approval must be remitted into a Taiwan bank account in New Taiwan Dollars or approved foreign exchange before incorporation, and must be attested by a Taiwan-certified public accountant through a capital verification report. The capital may not be withdrawn for purposes outside the approved business scope without an amended Investment Commission approval.

(TAIWAN): A meeting of the Board of Directors of [COMPANY] CO., LTD. The Chairperson confirmed that the Company had been organized as a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise limited-liability vehicle and that a quorum of directors was present. After deliberation, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted. 1. ARTICLES AND REGISTRATION:

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); local municipal and provincial tax revenue bureaus administer registration. Online portal: the unified China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) platform operated by the STA, supplemented by the China Customs Single Window for export clearance integration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the WFOE with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR); the resulting 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) is the statutory Tax Identification Number for all PRC tax filings. Step 2: AMR data is electronically pushed to the local STA bureau to complete automatic tax registration; the WFOE must finish supplemental taxpayer profile registration within 30 days of business license issuance, including accounting system details, statutory books, legal representative identity, place of business, and bank account information. Step 3: The WFOE files its opening bank account details and completes foreign exchange registration through a designated bank under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System administered by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange; this supports later foreign exchange repatriation evidence but is not a tax ID. Step 4: For VAT, the WFOE must register as a general VAT taxpayer if annual VAT taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000, or may voluntarily elect general VAT taxpayer status below that threshold; general VAT taxpayer status is a prerequisite for input VAT credit and export zero-rating. Step 5: A Taiwan or other foreign non-resident parent with no PRC establishment is not normally required to obtain a PRC TIN solely because it owns the WFOE; the WFOE handles Chinese corporate tax and withholding filings. If the foreign non-resident entity itself must file or claim treaty or cross-strait double taxation relief in China, it registers in the STA non-resident taxpayer module and receives an STA-issued tax identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a WFOE; it is mandatorily classified as a resident enterprise taxed at entity level. No hybrid mismatch entity-election mechanism exists. The only operational status election is between small-scale VAT taxpayer and general VAT taxpayer; general status election requires stricter invoicing and enables input credit and zero-rating. Treaty and cross-strait double taxation relief is claimed through non-resident withholding procedures and does not affect entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for compulsory tax registration: every PRC-registered WFOE must complete tax registration upon incorporation irrespective of revenue. Mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration arises when annual VAT taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000; below that, small-scale VAT taxpayer status applies, with a temporary monthly VAT exemption of CNY 100,000 for eligible small-scale taxpayers. The applicable PRC VAT rate for the WFOE's public relations and communication services is 6% when supplied domestically, while goods are generally subject to the 13% standard headline rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The PRC mandates electronic invoices through the national electronic invoice service platform (full digital electronic invoice system). VAT special invoices must be created using the taxpayer's tax control identity and transmitted in structured digital data format to the STA in real time. The STA validates a unique nationwide invoice number and digital fingerprint before the invoice can be used. Automated fiscal clearance is achieved through API-based integration for larger taxpayers, mandatory real-time uploads, the nationwide invoice verification platform, and anti-counterfeit controls using digital signatures, invoice code and number uniqueness, and cross-matching of invoice data with customs and bank foreign exchange records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A PRC general VAT taxpayer may apply the 0% export VAT rate to physical goods after actual departure from PRC customs territory, supported by the customs export declaration and receipt of foreign currency. For cross-border services, including public relations and media communications supplied to an overseas recipient in Taiwan, zero-rating applies only where the service is fully consumed outside the PRC and falls within the STA's enumerated zero-rating catalogue for cross-border taxable services, such as qualifying business process management or offshore service outsourcing; if not in that catalogue, the export service may be VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated. The WFOE must maintain service contracts, offshore consumption evidence, delivery records, bank payment receipts, and contemporaneous documentation showing no use or consumption within mainland China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) transmitted through the China Customs Single Window
Original or electronic Bill of Lading, air waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from PRC customs territory
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or the equivalent foreign exchange receipt or recordation voucher issued by a PRC-designated foreign exchange bank
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export contract matching the customs declaration data
Customs and tax data-pairing confirmation from the export tax refund information system
For cross-border services, substitute the customs declaration with a signed service agreement, offshore-consumption or use certificate, and bank payment evidence while retaining the FIRC
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities cross-check the customs exit messages, transport documents, bank foreign exchange receipt data, and VAT invoice data. If the zero-rating is unsubstantiated, the 0% rate is reversed, output VAT must be re-charged at the applicable domestic rate (6% for services or 13% for goods), corresponding input VAT credits are disallowed, a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% accrues on the unpaid tax, and administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the evaded or improperly refunded amount may be imposed. Intentional or false documentation can be referred for criminal investigation as export tax refund fraud or false VAT special invoice issuance, resulting in imprisonment and asset confiscation. The exporter must retain the substantiation pack for at least five years; fraudulent claims extend the statutory recovery period and permit retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains capital account convertibility restrictions while current account transactions remain generally convertible. Profit remittance to foreign parent entities requires SAFE approval, foreign exchange registration, and supporting documentation including audited financial statements, board resolutions, and proof of legitimate expenditure. Key hurdles include verification of fund utilization and compliance with SAFE filing timelines.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For service exports such as PR agency fees, no mandatory surrender of proceeds to domestic banks applies under the goods export regime. Foreign exchange settlement for service receipts must occur within five working days of receipt, with filing to the bank and SAFE using supporting documents including contracts, invoices, and proof of service delivery. Settlement occurs at prevailing market rates without fixed conversion ratios.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Legal constraints arise from Payment Services Regulations and AML requirements; offshore digital EMIs face restrictions on cross-border transfers without proper licensing and SAFE approval.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signatories must appear physically for KYC interviews and account opening at tier 1 banks. Remote opening is generally not permitted for WFOEs without prior SAFE and bank approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate structure chart, and notarized proof of ownership
Bank statements from parent entity, wire transfer records, and tax clearance certificates

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols involve parent company wire transfers to WFOE designated foreign exchange account via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Capital Contribution'. Verification requires SAFE filing within three working days post-transfer, supported by capital verification certificate from Chinese legal counsel.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for service settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. For PR agency disbursements, payments to overseas suppliers or clients must comply with service trade settlement rules, with FX registration required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps for long-term liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Responsible Persons and Major Shareholders Declaration (Director/UBO register filing under Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration and Records System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NTD 50,000 to NTD 5,000,000 for failure to file or false filing; repeated penalties may be imposed for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax finalization)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May of the following calendar year; if a non-calendar fiscal year is approved, within 5 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 1% per two days on unpaid tax, capped at 15%, plus daily interest; underreporting penalties up to two times the underpaid tax amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and, where applicable, CPA Audit Report (Company Act Article 20 submission)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Commercial Registration System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies) for companies with paid-in capital exceeding NTD 30 million; smaller companies must have audited or prepared statements available upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines on the responsible person under the Company Act for non-submission; MOEA may issue corrective orders and impose repeated fines until compliance is achieved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Operation Report for Approved Foreign Investment (Foreign National Investment reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after each fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year enterprises) for all companies with approved foreign investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report may trigger administrative correction orders and, under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, possible revocation of the investment approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder/Board Meeting Minutes and Statutory Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate record retained at the registered office; subject to inspection by MOEA or tax authorities on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a limited company, shareholder resolutions and board minutes must be finalized and recorded within 6 months after fiscal year-end; register entries updated within 15 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maintaining defective or incomplete statutory registers is subject to fines under the Company Act; continued violations may lead to court-ordered dissolution upon regulator or shareholder application.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Non-public companies with paid-in capital exceeding NTD 30,000,000 must have annual financial statements audited and certified by a certified public accountant; public companies and companies specified by MOEA or the Securities and Exchange Act are always subject to statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies: Taiwan-IFRS; non-public companies: Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) under the Business Entity Accounting Act, with optional early adoption of Taiwan-IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Non-public companies must file directors, supervisors, managers, and major shareholders (holding 10% or more) with MOEA during the annual window (1 January to 31 March). Any shareholding transfer or register change occurring during the year must be updated in the MOEA system within 15 days of the change, in addition to the regular annual confirmation.
